title: no/none/any; nothing/nobody etc.
subtitle: no / none / any; nothing / nobody / nowhere
summary: Use no + noun, none on its own and any after a negative verb, and use nothing/nobody/nowhere without adding a second negative.

lesson.heading: no + noun
lesson.text: We use **no** + noun (no bus, no shops etc.). **no** = not a or not any. You can also put **no** + noun at the beginning of a sentence.

examples.text: We had to walk home. There was **no** bus.
Sarah will have **no** trouble finding a job.
**No** reason was given for the change of plan.

lesson.heading: none - without a noun
lesson.text: We use **none** when there is no noun after it, or **none of** + the/this/it/them etc. After **none of** + a plural noun, the verb can be singular or plural.

examples.text: All the tickets have been sold. There are **none** left.
This money is all yours. **None of** it is mine.
**None of** the students **were** happy. or **None of** the students **was** happy.

lesson.heading: nothing / nobody / no-one / nowhere
lesson.text: You can use these words at the beginning of a sentence or alone, as answers to questions. You can also use them after a verb, especially after **be** and **have**.

examples.text: 'Where are you going?' '**Nowhere**. I'm staying here.'
The house is empty. There's **nobody** living there.

lesson.heading: nothing = not + anything
lesson.text: **nothing / nobody / nowhere** = not + anything / anybody / anywhere. With nothing/nobody etc. the verb stays positive - we do not add a negative verb (isn't, didn't etc.).

examples.note: = Jane didn't tell anybody about her plans.
= They don't have anywhere to live.

lesson.heading: they / them / their after nobody
lesson.text: After **nobody / no-one** you can use **they / them / their**, so you do not have to say 'he or she'.

examples.text: **No-one** did what I asked **them** to do.

left.label: no- (= not any)
examples: There was **no** bus, so we walked home.
'What do you want to eat?' '**Nothing**. I'm not hungry.'
It's a difficult job. **Nobody** wants to do it.

right.label: any- (= it doesn't matter which / what / who)
examples: You can take **any** bus. They all go to the centre.
I'm so hungry. I could eat **anything**.
It's a very easy job. **Anybody** can do it.

lesson.text: One negative is enough. Say I didn't see anybody or I saw nobody - never ~~I didn't see nobody~~.

exercises.prompt: We had to walk home. There were ___ taxis.
exercises.explanation: no + noun: There were no taxis (= there weren't any taxis).

exercises.prompt: We had to walk home. There weren't ___ taxis.
exercises.explanation: After a negative verb (weren't) we use any: There weren't any taxis.

exercises.prompt: 'How many eggs do we have?' '___. Shall I get some?'
exercises.explanation: With no noun after it, we use none (= no eggs).

exercises.prompt: We took a few pictures, but ___ of them were very good.
exercises.explanation: Before of them we use none, and the verb stays positive: none of them were very good.

exercises.prompt: Match each question with the short answer that uses none / nobody / nothing / nowhere.

pairs.left: What did you do at the weekend?
How much bread did you buy?
How much does it cost to get into the museum?

exercises.prompt: The bus was completely empty. There was ___ on it.
exercises.explanation: The verb is positive (was), so we need the negative word: There was nobody on it.

exercises.prompt: 'Who are you waiting for?' Give the same answer as 'Nobody', but with a negative verb + anybody.
exercises.explanation: not ... anybody = nobody: I'm not waiting for anybody.
The verb is already negative (don't know), so we use anything, not nothing.

exercises.statement: She didn't tell nobody about her plans.
exercises.explanation: She didn't tell anybody about her plans. (or She told nobody about her plans.) We do not use a negative verb with nobody.

exercises.statement: The accident looked bad, but fortunately nobody was seriously injured.

exercises.prompt: Let's go away. We can go ___ you like.
exercises.explanation: anywhere = it doesn't matter where: We can go anywhere you like.

exercises.prompt: Does the word in each sentence mean 'not any' or 'it doesn't matter which / what / who'?

items.text: There was no bus, so we walked home.
You can take any bus. They all go to the centre.
'What do you want to eat?' 'Nothing. I'm not hungry.'
I'm so hungry. I could eat anything.
It's a difficult job. Nobody wants to do it.
It's a very easy job. Anybody can do it.
